newsitem.title: JAPAN: YAMAICHI SEC SAYS TOP OFFICIALS QUIT OVER SCANDAL.
newsitem.headline: YAMAICHI SEC SAYS TOP OFFICIALS QUIT OVER SCANDAL.

text.p: Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd said on Monday that its chairman, president and nine other top executives were resigning to take responsibility for a racketeer payoff scandal.
In a statement, the company added that some of the resignations were also motivated by the brokerage's efforts to restructure its management in response to Japan's "Big Bang" financial reforms.
The statement said senior managing director Shohei Nozawa would replace current president Atsuo Miki.
A Yamaichi spokesman said earlier on Monday that the brokerage's chairman, president and five vice presidents were likely to resign over the high-profile racketeer payoff scandal.

Yamaichi, the smallest of Japan's "Big Four" brokerages, is suspected of making 79 million yen ($686,000) in illegal payoffs to Ryuichi Koike, the "sokaiya" racketeer at the heart of a financial scandal that has also ensnared Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd.
